GHSA-g2pg-6438-jwpf (withdrawn_at=null) and CVE-2026-22775 (cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED; NVD vulnStatus=Modified, not Rejected) both state that ArrayBuffer hydration expects a base64 string but does not check that assumption. Source-to-sink on the BIC tree: parse() JSON.parse's attacker input, unflatten/hydrate dispatches on value[0]==='ArrayBuffer', assigns const base64=value[1], and calls decode64(base64) with no typeof check (bbf86c2df544f3855603012b70d2be2200c7dbf3:src/parse.js). decode64/asciiToBinary then iterate i < data.length (src/base64.js explicitly 'Does not do any input validation'). A JSON object payload with a large .length that is not divisible by 4 skips data.replace and drives CPU work plus string-growth memory in the loop. The same unguarded ArrayBuffer case remains at v5.6.1 (5e07a67eda945b3ac2ebac26b18863beabee7357) and at fix-parent e46afa64dd2b25aa35fb905ba5d20cea63aabbf7.
